setup: git submodule update --init --recursive -q && cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo >/dev/null 2>&1 && cmake --build build -j8 2>&1 | tail -1
test: cmake -S external/ska -B build-judge -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo -DSKA_BUILD_DEMOS=OFF >/dev/null 2>&1 && cmake --build build-judge -j8 --target ska_gui_test >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo 'engine test build failed'; exit 3; }; cd external/ska && out=$(timeout 300 xvfb-run -a ../../build-judge/bin/ska_gui_test -tc='*keeps the other textures*' 2>&1); echo "$out" | tail -4; echo "$out" | grep -q 'Status: SUCCESS'
judge_note: The bug the owner hit: after a first battle, the next battle draws the player's Pokemon off its place (off screen). Root cause in the engine (a29b29ae, tangled into game commit 0c126b1): the texture of an image is shared by every texture of its file, so the battle's team slot resizing its image resized the sprites made from the same file. Judged by the fix's own engine test (hidden): before the fix 4 of 6 assertions fail (8 == 15), with it 6/6.

..CLAUDE.md:
# Smash & Dash


Pokémon fan game with real time battles, built on the ska engine (`external/ska`, with skalang in `external/ska/external/skalang`). The game is a library (`libGame`) loaded by the engine launcher `ska_main`.

## Build and run

```sh
cmake -S . -B build && cmake --build build -j8
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=build/lib build/bin/ska_main   # from the repository root (the game data and the "wd:" scripts are relative to it)
```

The build compiles every script (`smash_and_dash_scripts_check`): a script error fails the build, with its file and line.

Build time: about 2 min clean at `-j8` (6 cores, 12 threads: more jobs barely help), seconds for a game file, more for an engine header (included everywhere). The game sources compile while the engine links (object libraries `smash_and_dash_objects`, `smash_and_dash_worldgen`), the C++ standard headers are precompiled (ska `SKA_PRECOMPILED_HEADERS`), ccache is used when installed.

Battle simulation: `SAD_BATTLE_AUTOPLAY=1` makes the battle AI play the Pokemon of the player too; the debug log traces the battle (`Battle t=...`: decisions, skills used, hits, misses).

Script tests, headless (no window): `cd build && ctest`. They are `tests/*_test.miniska` (assertions: `Test = import "bind:std.native.test"`), run with the templates of the engine and game functions (default bodies) and the fakes of `tests/fakes` (ex: the engine keeps the game variables, `setNextRandom` chooses the random values). Add a test with a script change when the script has logic (rules, AI, helpers).

Web (browser, WebAssembly): `tools/web/build.sh [build-web]` (needs the Emscripten SDK: `source <emsdk>/emsdk_env.sh`, or `EMSDK=<emsdk>`; the first build builds the SDL3 libraries for the web), then `tools/web/serve.sh` serves `build-web/game/bin` to the local network (`http://<address>:8000`). The page is `src/web/shell.html`: it keeps the saves (`Data/Saves`) in the browser (IndexedDB). On the web: no thread, the browser calls each frame (`GameCore::run`), the renderer is WebGL (`opengles2`: no shaders), the game files are packed in `index.data` (the directories listed in `src/CMakeLists.txt`). The engine side is `external/ska/cmake/SkaWeb.cmake`. Online: each push on master builds it and publishes it on GitHub Pages (`.github/workflows/pages.yml`: https://scorbutics.github.io/SmashAndDash/).

Linux CI: `.github/workflows/linux.yml` (Debug and Release builds and the script tests, in an Ubuntu 26.04 container for its SDL3 packages).

Shaders: GLSL fragment shaders in `src/shaders/*.frag`, compiled during the build to `Shaders/<name>.frag.spv` (ska `ska_compile_shaders`, needs `glslangValidator`), loaded with `ska::Shader{ "./Shaders/<name>" }` (ska README "Shaders"). They need the SDL3 `gpu` renderer: without it the game draws without them. Ex: `battle.frag`, the post-processing of the battles (`GUIBattle`).

## Scripts

Read [SCRIPTING.md](SCRIPTING.md) (where scripts start, the functions given to them) and `external/ska/external/skalang/doc/LANGUAGE.md` (the language) before writing a script. The syntax differs from Ruby, JavaScript and Python. Keep skalang's rules: strong static typing, no implicit conversion, no null value.

- The generator is being ported to C++ (`src/src/Game/Gameplay/World/Generation`, plain C++ : it will make the world of a new game in the game, native and web), stage by stage, checked bit for bit against the Python one: `tools/worldgen/golden.py > tests/worldgen/golden.txt` (after a change of the Python generator), `ctest -R sad_worldgen`. Done: the noise, the climate (biomes, relief), the height before the villages; the villages (sites, growth, names), the distance to them, the biome weights and the mixes of the corners (`WorldPlan`); the roads (A*), the terrain (grounds, terraces, cleaned), the stairs, the places (`Terrain`); the tile of each block of the three layers (a tile is the text of its Python key), the blocks walked on, the villages decorated, the trees, the signs, the items, the rooms, the events, the light (`Layers`: the shapes of the drawn structures come from `Resources/Worldgen/shapes.txt`, `tools/worldgen/shapes.py`; the room templates are `Resources/Worldgen/rooms`). the chipsets (`Chipset`: the tiles drawn in each biome by Python, their collision masks (`tile_mask`, the `.png.mask` of each chipset: the solid parts of the tiles, 4 x 4 cells a tile, from the materials of their drawings: the rim of a cliff, a trunk; the walls of the game are these parts, ska README "Maps and tilesets"), `Resources/Worldgen/tiles.png` at one pixel per voxel, made by `tools/worldgen/atlas.py` after a change of the drawings or of the keys; C++ blends them per corner as PIL does and fills the cells; `Png`: a PNG reader and a BMP writer, plain C++). the files of a world (`Files`: the PNG writer deflates, a world is about 15 MB) and the worlds of the saves, generated by the game (`SaveSlots`, the title screen `StateTitle` and its loading screen, a step of `worldgen::WorldWriter` per frame; `SAD_SAVE=<name>` skips the title, `SAD_WORLD_SEED`; about 5 s, native and web). The Python generator stays the reference (the tests: `golden.txt` sums up every file of its seed 7 world).
- The maps are generated, a world per save, by the game in the save (`<save>/World/`, from `[World] seed`: SCRIPTING.md, "The world"); `tools/worldgen/worldgen.py --seed 7` writes the same world in `Data/Worlds/seed7/` (out of git; 8 x 8 chunks of 40 x 40 `w_*`, rooms `w_room_*`, a chipset per map in `Chipsets/`, biomes from a climate as in Minecraft, blended at their borders) (the game reads the maps of a save in its world: `[World] directory`, `MapDirectory` in `SavePaths.h`). `save1`: seed 7, `save2`: seed 42. Change the generator, not its output. A new kind of tile goes in the tile room too (`tools/worldgen/tileroom.py`, AGENTS.md), with its depth (`tile_base` in `worldgen.py`: flat, or how many blocks lower its object stands; written in `tiles.txt` and in the `.prop` of each chipset, the drawing order of the engine: ska README "Maps and tilesets"; a change of the format of the worlds: `worldgen::WorldVersion`, the older worlds of the saves are generated again). No story, no characters: only the capability scripts (`Levels/*.miniska`: surf, ledges, teleport, healing, shop, dialog, signs, items to find, rest beds).
- Map events: `<save>/World/<map>/<map>E.txt` (generated); the scripts they start stay in `Levels/`. Tile scripts: `Resources/Chipsets/tile_scripts/` (copied into the `Scripts/` of each generated chipset by the generator).
- The functions the game gives to the scripts are C++ modules in `src/src/Game/Script` (`game.dialog`, `game.character`, `game.map`, `game.party`, `game.interface`, `game.battle`), each declared by a template in `src/scripts/game.<name>.miniska`. Change the template with the C++ binding.
- A script only imported by other scripts (no `run` function) is listed in `GAME_SCRIPT_MODULES` (`src/CMakeLists.txt`).
- The texts are UTF-8 (the scripts, the data, the C++ literals, the worlds). `¤` is a line break in a message.

## Boundaries

C++ (ECS systems) owns the per frame work: the player and the characters walking around (`wander`, `patrol`) move block by block on the map (`Gameplay/Control/GridMovementSystem`, walls from the physics shapes; the wild Pokemon charge or flee the player by their attitude, `WildPokemonComponent`, and a battle starts when the trainer and one touch: `FightStartSystem`; they arrive flying in or out of a hideout, a drawing on a path then a wild Pokemon: `ArrivalSystem`; where they land, which hideout: the script `Data/Battle/arrivals.miniska`, started by `WorldState::spawnOne`), freely in battles; the drawing shows the entities between their last two logic states (`ska::FrameClock`); the real time battle simulation (`Gameplay/Fight`, a fighting game: each fighter has a `FighterComponent` (its side, its current opponent: the nearest one standing, who plays it, its attack, stun, K.O., cooldowns) iterated by `BattleDirectorSystem`, `BattleSystem`, `FighterSystem` and the skill systems; `BattleStage` shares the battle-wide state (time with its hit stops, arena, feedbacks, sounds, which fighter is the player's) with them and `GUIBattle`; `BattleHit` applies a hit (damage, `BattleEffects`: stat stages and statuses); the intro and the outro (`StateFight` tasks: `LeapTransition`, `PokeballTransition`; `BattlePhase::Outro`: the recall, the experience bar; then the map goes on without loading: `MapEvent::resume`, and the removed fighters are parked out of the physics space, which keeps their bodies); `BattleCameraSystem` moves and zooms the camera (the world is drawn zoomed below `WorldInterfacePriority`, the interface is not: `DrawableContainer::setWorldZoom`)): skills, movements, hits, end of the battle. The battle rules and the AI of the wild Pokemon are scripts (`Data/Battle`, called through `BattleRules`, each with a C++ fallback: `rules` statistics, damage, types, the softer hits of the wild Pokemon, the capture chance; `status`; `stages`; `encounters`; `skills` known; `rewards`; `ai`) : pure functions asked at events, never every frame (what applies every frame is asked when it changes and cached); the battle rolls the dice and gives them, so a seeded replay stays the same, the battle flow is scripted with `Battle.start`, the `battle.won` / `battle.lost` hooks and the steps of each battle (`Data/Battle/steps.miniska`: the director starts it at each step and waits for it; its banners, its dialogs). The screens that draw themselves each frame (the title `StateTitle`, the battle `GUIBattle`) use `Ui::Canvas` (`Graphic/GUI/Canvas.h`: texts, fills, the panels and bars of the theme `Theme`, the images of `Menu/default_theme` made by `tools/tilegen/ui.py`; `Ui::Layer`, `Ui::ChoiceList` for a menu with the keys and the mouse); the windows the player opens over the map (the team, the bag, the settings, the dialogs) are ska_gui windows (`GUIMap`: retained widgets, the mouse). ska_gui does not fit the first ones: no navigation with the keys (the web pad), its widgets keep their state while those screens change every frame (bars, shakes, banners that scale and fade, marks that follow the fighters, render effects). Scripts own the content and the sequencing: they call verbs and wait for their completion. A missing feature for scripts is a new verb in a game module (C++ and template), not polling from the script.

external/ska.CLAUDE.md:
# ska engine


2D game engine (SDL3, Chipmunk2D), ECS based, scripted with skalang (`external/skalang`; skalang, skabase and skalog are folders of this repository, not submodules: one commit changes them with the engine). Games (ex: Smash & Dash) embed it as a submodule and are libraries loaded by the `ska_main` launcher.

## Build and tests

```sh
cmake -S . -B build && cmake --build build -j8
build/bin/ska_core_test && build/bin/ska_scripting_test   # also ska_ai_test, ska_gui_test, ska_particle_test, ska_world_test
```

Options: `SKA_BUILD_DEMOS` (the physics demos; on when the engine is built alone, off in a game), `SKA_PHYSIC_HOMEMADE` (the homemade physics, deprecated, off: `ska_physic_chipmunk` replaces it), `SKA_PRECOMPILED_HEADERS` (the C++ standard headers precompiled for every C++ target, `cmake/SkaPrecompiledHeaders.cmake`; off on the web). ccache is used when it is installed (`cmake/SkaCompilerCache.cmake`, also included by the games).

Run the tests from the repository root: `ska_gui_test` loads `resources/Fonts` relative to the working directory (it needs a display: `xvfb-run` without one).

Web (Emscripten): `cmake/SkaWeb.cmake` (`ska_web_executable`: the game, the engine and SDL linked in one page; the functions loaded by name are found in a generated table, `DynamicLibraryStatic` in skabase), `tools/web/build_deps.sh <prefix>` builds the SDL3 libraries for it. On the web `SKA_PLATFORM_WEB` is defined (with `SKA_PLATFORM_LINUX`), there is no thread (the logger runs its commands at once) and the browser calls each frame (`GameCore::run`, `frame`).

Linux CI: `.github/workflows/linux.yml` (an Ubuntu 26.04 container: its SDL3 packages, lavapipe for the `gpu` renderer, xvfb).

Rerun `cmake -S . -B build` after adding a source file (the sources are globbed). The build also checks the module boundaries and the scripting test scripts.

## Modules

- `ska_core`: ECS (entities, components, systems), events, the `ScriptRunner` interface (`Core/ECS/Basics/Script`), the SDL3 calls (`SDLLibrary`, loaded at run time).
- Drawing: `ska_draw` (`SDLRenderer` on the SDL3 `gpu` driver when possible). Shaders: `Graphic/Shader.h`, GLSL compiled by `ska_compile_shaders` (`cmake/SkaShaders.cmake`), used by `RenderEffect::shader` and `Renderer::setScreenShader` (README "Shaders"). Zoom: `CameraSystem::zoomTo`/`setZoom`; the game calls `DrawableContainer::setWorldZoom(zoom, interfacePriority)`: the drawings below that priority are drawn in a texture stretched to the screen (`Renderer::beginWorld`/`endWorld`), the interface is not zoomed.
- `ska_draw`, `ska_gui`, `ska_audio`, `ska_particle`, `ska_ai`, `ska_physic_chipmunk`, `ska_world` (tile maps, chipsets): engine features.
- `ska_script`: `ScriptRefreshSystem`, the script triggers (map events, tiles) giving the scripts to the runner of their file extension.
- `ska_scripting`: the skalang runner (`ScriptVM`) and the engine functions given to the scripts (`EngineModule`, template `src/scripts/ska.engine.miniska`).

## Boundaries (checked at each build, `cmake/CheckBoundaries.cmake`)

- The engine modules know nothing about the scripting: they do not include skalang or `ska_scripting` headers. They start scripts through `ScriptRunner`.
- `ska_scripting` only depends on `ska_core` among the engine modules.
- C++ (ECS systems) owns the per frame work. Scripts own the content and the sequencing: they call verbs (move, wait, message...) and wait for their completion (a native function suspends the script, a completion event resumes it). Do not make scripts poll every frame.

## Scripting

- Scripts are skalang scripts: read `external/skalang/doc/LANGUAGE.md` before writing one. Keep skalang's rules: strong static typing, no implicit conversion, no null value.
- A native module is a `lang::Module` with a template script declaring its functions (`bind:<name>` → `<name>.miniska`). Update the template with the C++ binding: the static check (`skalang_check_scripts`, using `SKA_SCRIPT_TEMPLATES_DIR`) compiles the game scripts against the templates.
- A function that waits (ex: `Engine.wait`) suspends the script (`interpreter.suspend()`), and the VM resumes it when the action is over.
- Entities cross the boundary as handles (`EntityHandles`): never give a raw `EntityId` to a script, never use an `int` from a script as an `EntityId` without `handles.entity(...)`.
- Engine → scripts: `ScriptVM::call<T>` for a value needed right away (no wait allowed), hooks (`declareEvent`, `EngineModule::emit`) for events. Neither can run while a script step runs: calls throw, emits are deferred.

prompt:
Bug, seen while playing: after a first battle, in the next battle my Pokemon is drawn off its place — completely off screen — so it looks out of the battle from its very start. The first battle of a session is fine; it is from the second one on. It looks as if a sprite were reused with the wrong size or offset.

Find the cause and fix it there (not only its symptom in the battle screen), so that nothing drawn earlier changes how a sprite is drawn later.
